sheer.title: Sheer Curtain Fabrics
sheer.intro: Explore verified sheer fabrics for a light, layered window treatment.

sections.heading: Texture and daylight
sections.text: Open or fine constructions can soften the appearance of daylight. The weave, colour and actual sample determine the effect; a sheer is not a blackout curtain.

sections.heading: Living rooms and layered windows
sections.text: Consider a sheer for the lighter layer of a living room window, with a separate main curtain where more coverage is needed.

sections.heading: Privacy needs a real-room check
sections.text: Daytime screening does not guarantee privacy after dark. Assess the fabric against your own lighting and sightlines before deciding.

sections.heading: Pairing your layers
sections.text: Compare the sheer against the main fabric vertically. Confirm track clearance and the space for both layers to stack.

linen.title: Linen Curtain Fabrics
linen.intro: Explore verified linen and linen-blend records, checking each fabric's stated composition.

sections.heading: A relaxed woven appearance
sections.text: Linen is often chosen for visible texture and a less formal surface. A linen-look construction is not proof of linen content; check the supplier composition.

sections.heading: Styling a quieter room
sections.text: Compare a textured neutral with timber, painted walls and existing upholstery. Larger vertical samples show the overall effect better than small chips.

sections.heading: Light and lining
sections.text: Linen content alone does not establish privacy or light control. Ask about the exact weave, lining compatibility and intended window treatment.

sections.heading: Layering and care
sections.text: Pair the main fabric with a lighter sheer if the hanging system supports two layers. Follow the individual supplier's care instructions rather than assuming all linen blends behave alike.

velvet.title: Velvet Curtain Fabrics
velvet.intro: Explore verified velvet constructions and their available documented shades.

sections.heading: Pile, texture and direction
sections.text: Velvet's pile can change its apparent colour with viewing direction and lighting. Inspect the same sample from different positions before choosing a shade.

sections.heading: Creating a room focal point
sections.text: A deeper velvet shade can frame a window; a quieter colour can relate to upholstery. Consider the visible curtain area when the panels are open as well as closed.

sections.heading: Coverage is fabric-specific
sections.text: Do not infer a tested blackout rating from a heavy-looking fabric. Confirm the exact construction, lining and hanging arrangement.

sections.heading: Pairing with a sheer
sections.text: A lighter sheer can provide a visual contrast to a textured main curtain. Confirm hardware capacity and maintenance with the actual fabric specifications.

cotton.title: Cotton Curtain Fabrics
cotton.intro: Explore verified cotton and cotton-blend fabrics with composition recorded by the supplier.

sections.heading: Understand the construction
sections.text: Cotton describes a fibre rather than a single texture. Weave, finish and blend can produce very different surfaces and drapes.

sections.heading: Colours for lived-in rooms
sections.text: Compare fabric with the wall, flooring and upholstery in daylight and evening light. Choose a visual relationship rather than relying on a shade name alone.

sections.heading: Plan the level of coverage
sections.text: A cotton label does not establish opacity. Test a sample at the intended window and ask about suitable lining options.

sections.heading: Care and combinations
sections.text: Use the specific care label; do not assume a cotton curtain can be machine washed. Compare a sheer layer and confirm the heading and track arrangement before estimating fabric.

jacquard.title: Jacquard Curtain Fabrics
jacquard.intro: Explore verified woven-pattern curtain fabrics and their documented repeat information.

sections.heading: Pattern in the weave
sections.text: Jacquard refers to a patterned weaving approach, not a fibre composition. Read the exact composition and inspect how the pattern changes in folds.

sections.heading: Balance pattern and scale
sections.text: A larger motif reads differently across a narrow panel and a wide window. Compare the fabric with other patterned elements already in the room.

sections.heading: Light and appearance
sections.text: Backlighting may change how much of the woven pattern is visible. Check a physical sample at the window instead of inferring opacity from a photograph.

sections.heading: Layering and measurement
sections.text: A quieter sheer may let the main pattern lead. Ask for confirmed pattern repeats before estimating matching allowances; do not substitute a generic repeat value.

textured.title: Textured Curtain Fabrics
textured.intro: Explore verified fabrics chosen for visible woven or raised surface detail.

sections.heading: Look beyond a small swatch
sections.text: Texture can become more or less visible as fabric folds. A larger hanging sample helps compare the surface with flat upholstery and painted walls.

sections.heading: Room styling
sections.text: A textured neutral can add visual interest without a strong motif. Compare its undertone with flooring and the largest furniture pieces in the room.

sections.heading: Coverage and construction
sections.text: A tactile surface is not a technical specification. Confirm composition, light filtering, width and lining compatibility for the individual fabric.

sections.heading: A considered pairing
sections.text: Compare the main fabric and sheer side by side in the intended light. Confirm each layer independently and use their actual care guidance.

silk.title: Silk Curtain Fabrics
silk.intro: Explore supplier-confirmed silk constructions only when their composition and details are documented.

sections.heading: Surface and composition
sections.text: A lustrous appearance alone does not establish silk content. Read the supplier composition and inspect how the surface changes under directional light.

sections.heading: A formal or restrained direction
sections.text: Compare sheen with the room's finishes and lighting. A simple heading can produce a different visual effect from a more gathered treatment.

sections.heading: Check the window conditions
sections.text: Discuss exposure, lining and the exact fabric's suitability with the supplier. Do not infer durability or light control from a material name.

sections.heading: Care and layering
sections.text: Follow the individual care instructions. If pairing with a sheer, confirm hardware, stacking space and how both samples appear together.
